title.zh: 卷一百八十三 列傳第一百零八 畢崔劉陸鄭朱韓
title.en: Volume 183 Biographies 108: Bi, Cui, Liu, Lu, Zheng, Zhu, Han
title.raw: 卷一百八十三 列傳第一百零八 畢崔劉陸鄭朱韓 Volume 183 Biographies 108: Bi, Cui, Liu, Lu, Zheng, Zhu, Han

sentences.zh: 畢崔劉陸鄭朱韓

translations.literal: Bi, Cui, Liu, Lu, Zheng, Zhu, Han.
translations.idiomatic: Bi, Cui, Liu, Lu, Zheng, Zhu, and Han.

sentences.zh: 畢諴，字存之，黃門監構從孫。

translations.literal: Bi Yan, style name Cunzhi, was a collateral descendant of the Yellow Gate Supervisor Bi Gou.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Yan, whose courtesy name was Cunzhi, was a collateral descendant of Bi Gou, Supervisor of the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 構弟栩，生淩，淩生勻，世失官，為鹽估。

translations.literal: Gou's younger brother Xu begot Ling; Ling begot Yun. For generations the family lost office and became salt brokers.
translations.idiomatic: Gou's younger brother Xu had a son Ling, and Ling had a son Yun. For generations the line had fallen from office, and they made their living as salt merchants.

sentences.zh: 勻生諴，蚤孤。

translations.literal: Yun fathered Yan, who lost his father early.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was Yan's father; Yan was orphaned while still young.

sentences.zh: 夜然薪讀書，母恤其疲，奪火使寐，不肯息，遂通經史，工辭章。

translations.literal: At night he burned firewood to read. His mother, pitying his weariness, seized the fire and made him sleep, but he would not rest and eventually mastered the classics and histories and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He would read at night by burning firewood for light. When his mother, worried that he was exhausting himself, took away the fire and made him sleep, he still would not stop. In time he mastered the classics and histories and became accomplished in literary composition.

sentences.zh: 性端愨，不妄與人交。

translations.literal: His nature was upright and cautious; he did not associate with people casually.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright and reserved by nature and did not enter friendships lightly.

sentences.zh: 大和中，舉進士、書判拔萃，連中。

translations.literal: In the Dahe era he passed the jinshi examination and the "outstanding in document analysis" selection, succeeding in both in succession.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dahe reign he passed both the jinshi examination and the special "outstanding document analysis" selection, winning each in turn.

sentences.zh: 辟忠武杜悰幕府。

translations.literal: He was recruited into the staff of Du Cong, military governor of Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was invited to serve on the staff of Du Cong, governor of Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 悰領度支，表為巡官，又從辟淮南，入拜侍御史。

translations.literal: When Cong headed the revenue bureau, Yan was listed as an inspection officer. He again followed Cong to Huainan, then entered court as remonstrating censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Cong took charge of the Directorate of Revenue, Yan was recommended as an inspection officer. He followed Cong again to Huainan and later entered the capital as a remonstrating censor.

sentences.zh: 李德裕始與悰同輔政，不協，故出悰劍南東川節度使。

translations.literal: Li Deyu had at first served as chief minister alongside Cong but they did not get along, so Cong was sent out as military commissioner of Jiannan Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu had first served as chief minister together with Cong, but the two fell out, and Cong was therefore sent out as military commissioner of Jiannan Dongchuan.

sentences.zh: 故吏惟諴餞訊如平日，德裕忌之，出為慈州刺史。

translations.literal: Of his former staff only Yan saw him off and inquired after him as on ordinary days. Deyu resented this and had him sent out as prefect of Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Among his former subordinates, only Yan came to see him off and asked after his welfare as though nothing had changed. Deyu took offense at this and had Yan sent out as prefect of Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 累官駕部員外郎、倉部郎中。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Vice Director of the Carriages Bureau and Director of the Granary Department.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced through the ranks to Vice Director of the Carriages Bureau and Director of the Granary Department.

sentences.zh: 故事，要家勢人，以倉、駕二曹為辱，諴沛然如處美官，無異言。

translations.literal: By precedent powerful families regarded the Granary and Carriages bureaus as demeaning. Yan took them with full satisfaction as if in fine posts, without complaint.
translations.idiomatic: By custom men of powerful families treated the Granary and Carriages bureaus as humiliating posts, but Yan accepted them with evident satisfaction, as though they were prized offices, and never uttered a word of complaint.

sentences.zh: 宰相知之，以職方郎中兼侍御史知雜事，召入翰林為學士。

translations.literal: The chief minister took note and appointed him Director of Military Appointments while also serving as remonstrating censor handling miscellaneous matters, then summoned him into the Hanlin Academy as academician.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief minister learned of this, he appointed Yan Director of Military Appointments while also making him a remonstrating censor in charge of miscellaneous matters, and then summoned him into the Hanlin Academy as an academician.

sentences.zh: 党項擾河西，宣宗嘗召訪邊事，諴援質古今，條破羌狀甚悉，帝悅曰：「吾將擇能帥者，孰謂頗、牧在吾禁署，卿為朕行乎。

translations.literal: When the Tangut troubled Hexi, Emperor Xuanzong once summoned him to inquire about border affairs. Yan cited ancient and modern examples and laid out the situation for breaking the Qiang in great detail. The emperor said with pleasure: "I shall choose a capable commander—who says Pang and Mu are in my inner court? Will you go for me, sir?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Tangut were raiding along the Hexi frontier, Emperor Xuanzong once summoned Yan to consult him on border affairs. Yan drew on ancient and modern precedents and set out a detailed plan for defeating the Qiang. Delighted, the emperor said, "I mean to choose a capable commander—who would have thought that Pang and Mu were right here in my inner court? Will you go on my behalf, sir?"

sentences.zh: 」諴唯唯，即拜刑部侍郎，出為邠寧節度、河西供軍安撫使。

translations.literal: " Yan assented repeatedly and was immediately appointed Vice Minister of Punishments and sent out as commissioner of Binning and envoy to pacify and supply the army on the Hexi frontier.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan assented again and again. He was at once appointed Vice Minister of Punishments and sent out as military commissioner of Binning and envoy to pacify the frontier and supply the Hexi armies.

sentences.zh: 諴到軍，遣吏懷諭，羌人皆順向。

translations.literal: When Yan reached the army he sent clerks with persuasion in their bosoms; the Qiang all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan arrived at his command, he sent officials bearing conciliatory messages, and the Qiang all came over to the Tang side.

sentences.zh: 時戍兵常苦調饟乏，諴募士置屯田，歲收谷三十萬斛，以省度支經費，詔書嘉美。

translations.literal: At that time garrison troops often suffered from lack of transported provisions. Yan recruited men to establish military colonies and collected three hundred thousand bushels of grain yearly, saving expenditure for the revenue bureau. An edict praised this.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the garrison troops were constantly short of transported rations. Yan recruited men to establish military colonies and harvested three hundred thousand bushels of grain each year, easing the burden on the revenue directorate. An imperial edict commended his work.

sentences.zh: 俄徙昭義，又遷河東。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to Zhaoyi, then transferred to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Zhaoyi, and then again to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 河東尤近胡，復脩杷頭七十烽，謹候虜，寇不敢入。

translations.literal: Hedong was especially close to the barbarians. He rebuilt seventy beacon towers at Batou, watched the enemy closely, and raiders dared not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong lay especially close to the northern tribes. Yan restored seventy beacon towers at Batou, kept strict watch on the enemy, and raiders no longer dared cross the border.

sentences.zh: 懿宗立，遷宣武節度使，召為戶部尚書，判度支。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yizong succeeded, Yan was transferred to Xuanwu commissioner, then summoned as Minister of Revenue presiding over the budget.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yizong came to the throne, Yan was made military commissioner of Xuanwu, then recalled to serve as Minister of Revenue with charge of the budget.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以禮部尚書同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Minister of Rites and concurrently Co-Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Minister of Rites and concurrent Co-Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 再期，固稱疾，改兵部尚書，罷。

translations.literal: After a second year of the term he firmly claimed illness, was changed to Minister of War, and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of a second year in office he insisted that he was ill, was reassigned as Minister of War, and then removed from the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 旋兼平章事節度河中。

translations.literal: Soon he also served as co-director while commissioner of Hedongzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he again held the title of co-director while serving as military commissioner of Hedongzhong.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十二。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 諴於吏術尤所長，既貴，所得祿奉，養護宗屬之乏，無間然。

translations.literal: Yan was especially skilled in administration. Once elevated, his salary and stipends went to support needy clansmen without distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was especially gifted in the arts of administration. After he rose to high rank, he used his salary and stipends to support needy members of his clan without making distinctions among them.

sentences.zh: 始，諴被知於宣宗，嘗許以相。

translations.literal: At first, when Xuanzong noticed him, he had promised him the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong first took notice of him, the emperor had even promised him the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 令狐忌之，自邠寧凡三徙，不得還。

translations.literal: Linghu Tao bore him ill will. From Binning he was transferred three times and could not return.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Tao came to resent him. After leaving Binning, Yan was transferred three times in succession and was never able to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 諴思有以結，至太原，求麗姝盛飾使獻。

translations.literal: Yan thought to win him over. Reaching Taiyuan, he sought beautiful women richly adorned to present.
translations.idiomatic: Yan looked for a way to win Tao over. When he reached Taiyuan, he sought out beautiful women, had them richly adorned, and sent them as a gift.

sentences.zh: 曰：「太原於我無分，今以是餌，將破吾族矣。

translations.literal: Tao said: "Taiyuan has no share with me. Now if you bait me with this you will destroy my clan."
translations.idiomatic: Tao said, "Taiyuan has nothing to do with me. If you try to lure me with this now, you will bring ruin on my whole clan."

sentences.zh: 」不受。

translations.literal: " He would not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: " He refused to accept them.

sentences.zh: 使者留於邸，諴亦放之。

translations.literal: The messenger lodged them at the residence; Yan also released them.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy left the women at Yan's residence, but Yan set them free as well.

sentences.zh: 太醫李玄伯者，帝所喜，以錢七十萬聘之，夫婦日自進食，得其歡心，乃進之帝，嬖幸冠後宮。

translations.literal: The imperial physician Li Xuanbo was favored by the emperor. With seven hundred thousand cash Yan hired him; husband and wife daily brought food themselves to win his favor, then presented him to the emperor, and he became the favorite above all the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial physician Li Xuanbo was a man the emperor favored. Yan paid seven hundred thousand cash to retain him. Husband and wife came each day to serve food with their own hands until they had won his goodwill, then presented him to the emperor, and Xuanbo became the foremost favorite of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 玄伯又治丹劑以進，帝餌之，疽生於背。

translations.literal: Xuanbo also prepared elixir pills to present; the emperor took them and a carbuncle grew on his back.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbo also prepared elixir pills and presented them to the throne. The emperor ingested them, and a festering sore developed on his back.

sentences.zh: 懿宗立，收玄伯及方士王嶽、虞芝等，俱誅死。

translations.literal: When Yizong succeeded, Xuanbo and the alchemists Wang Yue and Yu Zhi were arrested and all executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yizong came to the throne, Xuanbo and the alchemists Wang Yue and Yu Zhi were arrested and all put to death.

sentences.zh: 崔彥昭，字思文，其先清河人。

translations.literal: Cui Yanhao, style name Siwen; his ancestors were men of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yanhao, whose courtesy name was Siwen, came from a family originally of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 淹貫儒術，擢進士第。

translations.literal: Thoroughly versed in Confucian learning, he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply versed in Confucian learning, he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 數應帥鎮辟奏，於吏治精明，所至課最。

translations.literal: Several times he answered recruitment by regional commanders. In governance he was sharp, and wherever he went his performance ratings were top.
translations.idiomatic: He answered the recruitment calls of several military governors. In administration he was exceptionally capable, and wherever he served his performance evaluations ranked first.

sentences.zh: 累進戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He rose to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted step by step to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 繇河陽節度使徙河東。

translations.literal: From Heyang commissioner he was moved to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred from military commissioner of Heyang to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 先是，沙陀諸部多犯法，彥昭撫循有威惠，三年，境內大治，耆老叩闕願留，詔可。

translations.literal: Before this the Shatuo tribes had often broken the law. Yanhao governed them with authority and kindness. In three years the territory was greatly pacified; elders knocked at the palace gates asking him to remain, and the edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Before this the Shatuo tribes had frequently broken the law. Yanhao governed them with a balance of sternness and kindness, and within three years the region was thoroughly pacified. The elders came to the capital to petition that he be allowed to stay, and the throne granted their request.

sentences.zh: 僖宗立，授兵部侍郎、諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong succeeded he was made Vice Minister of War and Commissioner for Salt and Iron Transport on all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong came to the throne, Yanhao was appointed Vice Minister of War and Commissioner for Salt and Iron Transport on all circuits.

sentences.zh: 俄同中書門下平章事，仍判度支。

translations.literal: Soon he was Co-Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, still presiding over the budget.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he became Co-Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery while continuing to preside over the budget.

sentences.zh: 初，楊收、路巖、韋保衡皆坐朋比賄賂得罪死，蕭仿秉政，矯革之，而彥昭協力，故百職修舉，察不至苛。

translations.literal: Earlier Yang Shou, Lu Yan, and Wei Baoheng had all been punished by death for faction and bribery. Xiao Fang held government and corrected this, and Yanhao cooperated, so every office was restored and oversight did not become harsh.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yang Shou, Lu Yan, and Wei Baoheng had all been condemned to death for forming factions and taking bribes. When Xiao Fang took charge of government he set about correcting these abuses, and Yanhao worked in concert with him, so that every office was put back in order and oversight never became oppressive.

sentences.zh: 不六月，遷門下侍郎。

translations.literal: In less than six months he was promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In less than six months he was promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 帝因下詔暴收等過惡，申勵丁寧，以成其美。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore issued an edict exposing the crimes of Shou and others, exhorting with care to complete their reform.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore issued an edict exposing the crimes of Shou and the others, urging the court with repeated admonitions so that their reforms might be brought to completion.

sentences.zh: 彥昭雖宰相，退朝侍母膳，與家人齒，順色柔聲，在左右無違，士人多其孝。

translations.literal: Though Yanhao was chancellor, when he left court he waited on his mother's meals and ate with his family in turn, with gentle expression and soft voice, never disobeying those beside him; scholars praised his filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Although Yanhao was a chancellor, after leaving court he would wait on his mother at meals and take his place among the family in proper order, always with a gentle look and a quiet voice, never defying those around him. Men of learning widely praised his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 與王凝外昆弟也。

translations.literal: He was a cousin by marriage of Wang Ning.
translations.idiomatic: He was related to Wang Ning as a cousin by marriage.

sentences.zh: 凝大中初先顯，而彥昭未仕，嘗見凝，凝倨不冠帶，嫚言曰：「不若從明經舉。

translations.literal: Ning had risen early in the Dazhong era while Yanhao was still without office. Once Yanhao visited Ning, who was haughty without cap or sash and insulted him, saying: "You might as well try the Mingjing examination."
translations.idiomatic: Ning had risen to prominence early in the Dazhong era while Yanhao had yet to take office. On one occasion Yanhao called on him. Ning received him arrogantly without cap or sash and spoke contemptuously, saying, "You would do better to try the Mingjing examination."

sentences.zh: 」彥昭為憾。

translations.literal: " Yanhao harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: " The remark left Yanhao deeply resentful.

sentences.zh: 至是，凝為兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: By now Ning was Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: By this time Ning had become Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 母聞彥昭相，敕婢多制屨襪，曰：「王氏妹必與子皆逐，吾將共行。

translations.literal: When his mother heard Yanhao was chancellor she ordered maids to make many shoes and socks, saying: "Wang's sister will surely be driven out together with her son; I shall go with them."
translations.idiomatic: When Ning's mother heard that Yanhao had become chancellor, she ordered the maids to make many pairs of shoes and socks, saying, "Wang's sister-in-law will surely be driven out together with her son. I shall go into exile with them."

sentences.zh: 」彥昭聞之，泣且拜，不敢為怨。

translations.literal: " When Yanhao heard this he wept and bowed and dared not harbor grievance.
translations.idiomatic: " When Yanhao heard of this, he wept and bowed in submission and did not dare to act on his resentment.

sentences.zh: 而凝竟免。

translations.literal: Yet in the end Ning escaped dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, however, Ning was spared dismissal after all.

sentences.zh: 伶人李可及為懿宗所寵，橫甚，彥昭奏逐，死嶺南。

translations.literal: The entertainer Li Keji was favored by Yizong and was overbearing in the extreme. Yanhao memorialized to exile him, and he died in Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: The performer Li Keji was a favorite of Yizong and behaved with outrageous arrogance. Yanhao submitted a memorial calling for his banishment, and Keji died in Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 累拜兼尚書右僕射，以疾去位，授太子太傅，卒。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to concurrent Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, then left office for illness, was given Crown Prince Grand Tutor, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in stages to concurrent Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, then left office because of illness, was appointed Crown Prince Grand Tutor, and died.

sentences.zh: 劉鄴，字漢藩，潤州句容人。

translations.literal: Liu Ye, style name Hanfan, a man of Jurong in Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ye, whose courtesy name was Hanfan, was a native of Jurong in Run Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父三復，以善文章知名。

translations.literal: His father Sanfu was renowned for skill in literature.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liu Sanfu was known for his literary talent.

sentences.zh: 少孤，母病廢，三復丐粟以養。

translations.literal: Ye lost his father young; his mother was crippled by illness, and Sanfu begged grain to support her.
translations.idiomatic: Ye was orphaned while still young. His mother was disabled by illness, and Sanfu begged for grain to support her.

sentences.zh: 李德裕為浙西觀察使，奇其文，表為掌書記。

translations.literal: When Li Deyu was Zhexi observation commissioner he admired Sanfu's writing and recommended him as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Deyu served as observation commissioner of Zhexi, he admired Sanfu's writing and recommended him as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 德裕三領浙西及劍南、淮南，未嘗不從。

translations.literal: Deyu thrice led Zhexi as well as Jiannan and Huainan; Sanfu never failed to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu thrice held command over Zhexi, Jiannan, and Huainan, and Sanfu never failed to follow him.

sentences.zh: 會昌時，位宰相，擢三復刑部侍郎、弘文館學士。

translations.literal: In the Huichang era when he reached chancellor he promoted Sanfu to Vice Minister of Punishments and Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huichang era, when Deyu rose to the chancellorship, he promoted Sanfu to Vice Minister of Punishments and made him a scholar of the Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 鄴六七歲能屬辭，德裕憐之，使與其子共師學。

translations.literal: Ye at six or seven could compose; Deyu pitied him and had him study with his sons under the same masters.
translations.idiomatic: When Ye was only six or seven he could already compose texts. Deyu took pity on him and had him study under the same teachers as his own sons.

sentences.zh: 德裕既斥，鄴無所依，去客江湖間。

translations.literal: When Deyu was dismissed Ye had nowhere to rely on and left to wander as a guest among the rivers and lakes.
translations.idiomatic: After Deyu was dismissed from office, Ye had no patron to rely on and went off to wander as a guest among the rivers and lakes.

sentences.zh: 陜虢高元裕表署推官，高少逸又辟鎮國幕府。

translations.literal: Gao Yuanyu of Shan-Guo listed him as aide; Gao Shaoyi also recruited him to the Zhenguo staff.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yuanyu of Shan-Guo appointed him to his staff as an aide, and Gao Shaoyi later recruited him into the staff of Zhenguo.

sentences.zh: 咸通初，擢左拾遺，召為翰林學士，賜進士第。

translations.literal: Early in Xiantong he was promoted to Left Remonstrator, summoned as Hanlin academician, and granted jinshi rank.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiantong era he was promoted to Left Remonstrator, summoned into the Hanlin Academy as an academician, and granted the rank of jinshi.

sentences.zh: 歷中書舍人，遷承旨。

translations.literal: He passed through Secretariat Drafter and was promoted to chief academician.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a Secretariat drafter and was then promoted to chief academician of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 鄴傷德裕以朋黨抱誣死海上，令狐久當國，更數赦，不為還官爵。

translations.literal: Ye grieved that Deyu died at sea falsely charged as a factionalist. Linghu long held power and through several amnesties would not restore his office and titles.
translations.idiomatic: Ye grieved that Deyu had died at sea, falsely condemned as a factionalist. Linghu Tao had long held power, and through one amnesty after another he refused to restore Deyu's offices and titles.

sentences.zh: 至懿宗立，去位，鄴乃申直其冤，復官爵，世高其義。

translations.literal: When Yizong succeeded and left office, Ye then petitioned to rectify his wrong and restored office and titles; the age highly honored this righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When Yizong came to the throne and Tao left office, Ye petitioned to rectify Deyu's wrong and had his offices and titles restored. His contemporaries greatly honored this act of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 進戶部侍郎、諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue and Commissioner for Salt and Iron Transport.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue and Commissioner for Salt and Iron Transport on all circuits.

sentences.zh: 以禮部尚書同中書門下平章事，判度支。

translations.literal: As Minister of Rites he was Co-Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery presiding over the budget.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of Rites and concurrent Co-Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery with charge of the budget.

sentences.zh: 僖宗嗣位，再遷尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: When Xizong succeeded he was twice promoted to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Xizong succeeded to the throne, Ye was twice promoted to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，韋保衡、路巖與鄴同秉政，為跡親。

translations.literal: At first Wei Baoheng and Lu Yan wielded government with Ye and were close in their tracks.
translations.idiomatic: At first Wei Baoheng and Lu Yan held power together with Ye, and the three were closely allied.

sentences.zh: 俄而蕭仿、崔彥昭得相，罷鄴為淮南節度使、同平章事。

translations.literal: Soon Xiao Fang and Cui Yanhao became chancellors and Ye was removed to Huainan commissioner and co-director.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xiao Fang and Cui Yanhao gained the chancellorship, and Ye was removed to serve as military commissioner of Huainan with the concurrent title of co-director.

sentences.zh: 黃巢方熾，詔高駢代之，徙節度鳳翔，固辭，還左僕射。

translations.literal: Huang Chao was raging; the edict had Gao Pian replace him. He was moved to Fengxiang commissioner, firmly declined, and returned to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao's rebellion was at its height, and an edict appointed Gao Pian to replace him. Ye was transferred to military commissioner of Fengxiang, but he firmly declined the post and returned to his former office as Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 帝西狩，追乘輿不及，與崔沆、豆盧瑑匿將軍張直方家，賊捕急，三人不肯臣，俱見殺。

translations.literal: When the emperor went west on campaign Ye could not catch the imperial carriage. With Cui Hang and Doulu Zuan he hid at the home of General Zhang Zhifang. When bandits pressed the capture the three men refused to submit and were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went west on campaign, Ye could not overtake the imperial carriage. Together with Cui Hang and Doulu Zuan he hid in the home of General Zhang Zhifang. When the rebels pressed their search, the three men refused to submit and were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 豆盧瑑者，字希真，河南人。

translations.literal: Doulu Zuan, style name Xizhen, a man of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Doulu Zuan, whose courtesy name was Xizhen, was a native of Henan.

sentences.zh: 仕歷翰林學士、戶部侍郎，與崔沆皆拜同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He served as Hanlin academician and Vice Minister of Revenue; with Cui Hang both were appointed Co-Directors of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In his career he rose through the offices of Hanlin academician and Vice Minister of Revenue. He and Cui Hang were both appointed Co-Directors of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 是日，宣告於廷，大風雷雨拔樹。

translations.literal: That day when it was announced in court a great wind and thunderstorm uprooted trees.
translations.idiomatic: On the day their appointments were announced in court, a violent wind and thunderstorm uprooted trees.

sentences.zh: 未幾，及禍。

translations.literal: Before long they met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they met with disaster.

sentences.zh: 初，咸通中，有治歷者工言禍福，或問：「比宰相多不至四五，謂何？

translations.literal: Earlier in the Xiantong era there was a calendar expert skilled at speaking of fortune and disaster. Someone asked: "Lately many chancellors do not reach four or five years—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Xiantong era, there was a man skilled in calendrical science who was adept at foretelling fortune and disaster. Someone asked him, "In recent times many chancellors do not remain in office even four or five years—what does this mean?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「紫微方災，然其人又將不免。

translations.literal: " He answered: "The Purple Forbidden is about to suffer calamity, yet those persons themselves will also not escape."
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "Calamity is about to strike the Purple Forbidden Palace, yet those men themselves will not escape it either."

sentences.zh: 」後楊收、韋保衡、路巖、盧攜、劉鄴、於琮、彖與沆，皆不得終雲。

translations.literal: " Later Yang Shou, Wei Baoheng, Lu Yan, Lu She, Liu Ye, Yu Cong, Li Tan, and Cui Hang—all did not end well, as he said.
translations.idiomatic: " Later Yang Shou, Wei Baoheng, Lu Yan, Lu She, Liu Ye, Yu Cong, Li Tan, and Cui Hang—none of them came to a peaceful end, just as he had foretold.

sentences.zh: 陸扆，字祥文，宰相贄族孫。

translations.literal: Lu Yi, style name Xiangwen, a collateral descendant of Chancellor Lu Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yi, whose courtesy name was Xiangwen, was a collateral descendant of the chancellor Lu Zan.

sentences.zh: 客於陜，遂為陜人。

translations.literal: He lodged in Shan and thus became a man of Shan.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long resided in Shan, and he came to be regarded as a native of that region.

sentences.zh: 光啟二年，從僖宗幸山南，擢進士第，累進翰林學士、中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangqi he followed Xizong to the south of the mountains, passed the jinshi examination, and rose through Hanlin academician and Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangqi he followed Emperor Xizong to the south of the mountains, passed the jinshi examination, and rose step by step to Hanlin academician and Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 扆工屬辭，敏速若註射然，一時書命，同僚自以為不及，昭宗優遇之。

translations.literal: Yi was skilled at composition and as swift as if annotating and shooting; for a time in court documents his colleagues knew they could not match him, and Zhaozong favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was skilled at literary composition and wrote with a speed that seemed almost effortless. For a time, whenever court documents were drafted, his colleagues knew they could not keep pace with him, and Emperor Zhaozong treated him with special favor.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗作賦，詔學士皆和，獨扆最先就。

translations.literal: The emperor once composed a fu and ordered the academicians all to match it; only Yi finished first.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion the emperor composed a fu and ordered all the academicians to write matching pieces. Yi alone finished first.

sentences.zh: 帝覽之，嘆曰：「貞元時，陸贄、吳通玄兄弟善內廷文書，後無繼者，今朕得之。

translations.literal: The emperor reading it sighed: "In the Zhenyuan era Lu Zan and the Wu brothers Tongxuan were skilled at inner-court documents; afterward none succeeded—now I have found one."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor read his composition, he sighed and said, "In the Zhenyuan era Lu Zan and the Wu brothers, Tongxuan and Tongming, were masters of inner-court documents. After them there was no successor—until now, when I have found one in you."

sentences.zh: 」始，得舉進士時，方遷幸，而六月榜出。

translations.literal: " When he first passed the jinshi examination the court was on the move in flight, and the roster came out in the sixth month.
translations.idiomatic: " When he first passed the jinshi examination, the court was still on the move in flight, and the examination roster was issued in the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 至是，每甚暑，它學士輒戲曰：「造榜天也。

translations.literal: From then on whenever it was very hot the other academicians would jest: "The roster-making heaven."
translations.idiomatic: From then on, whenever the weather grew intensely hot, the other academicians would jest, calling him "Heaven Who Makes the Rosters."

sentences.zh: 」以譏扆進非其時。

translations.literal: " To mock that Yi's advancement came at the wrong season.
translations.idiomatic: " They did this to mock the fact that Yi's rise had come at an inauspicious season.

sentences.zh: 累為尚書左丞，封嘉興縣男。

translations.literal: He rose repeatedly to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and was enfeoffed as Baron of Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and was enfeoffed as Baron of Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 徙戶部侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He was moved to Vice Minister of Revenue and Co-Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue and appointed Co-Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 故事，自三省得宰相，有光署錢，留為宴資，學士院未始有。

translations.literal: By precedent when one reached chancellor from the Three Departments there was "glory commission" money kept for feast funds; the Academy of Academicians had never had it.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, when a man became chancellor after rising through the Three Departments, he received a "glory commission" payment set aside for celebratory feasts, but the Hanlin Academy had never received such a payment.

sentences.zh: 至扆，送光院錢五十萬，以榮近司。

translations.literal: When Yi [became chancellor], he sent five hundred thousand to the Academy to honor the nearby office.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi became chancellor, he sent five hundred thousand cash to the Academy as a glory payment, thereby honoring the office he had just left.

sentences.zh: 進中書侍郎，判戶部。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat presiding over the Revenue Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat with charge of the Revenue Ministry.

sentences.zh: 嗣覃王以兵伐鳳翔，扆諫曰：「國步方安，不宜加兵近輔，必為它盜所乘，無益也。

translations.literal: When the Siyu King raised troops to attack Fengxiang, Yi remonstrated: "The nation's fortune is just settling; it is not fitting to add troops near the capital—other bandits will surely take advantage, to no benefit."
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Siyu raised an army to attack Fengxiang, Yi remonstrated, saying, "The fortunes of the state have only just begun to settle. It is not fitting to bring additional troops so close to the capital. Other marauders will surely take advantage of the situation, and nothing will be gained."

sentences.zh: 且親王而屬軍事，必有後害。

translations.literal: Moreover a royal prince taking charge of military affairs must bring later harm.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when a royal prince is placed in command of military affairs, harm is sure to follow afterward.

sentences.zh: 」帝顧軍興，責扆沮撓，貶峽州刺史。

translations.literal: " The emperor, intent on the military campaign, blamed Yi for obstruction and demoted him to prefect of Xia.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor, bent on pressing the military campaign, blamed Yi for obstruction and demoted him to prefect of Xia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 師果敗。

translations.literal: The army indeed was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign ended in defeat.

sentences.zh: 久之，授工部尚書。

translations.literal: After a long time he was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 從天子自華州還，以兵部尚書復當國，封吳郡公。

translations.literal: Following the Son of Heaven's return from Hua Prefecture, as Minister of War he again held the government and was enfeoffed Duke of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned from Hua Prefecture, Yi again took charge of government as Minister of War and was enfeoffed as Duke of Wu.

sentences.zh: 天復初，帝密語韓偓曰：「陸扆、裴贄孰忠於我？

translations.literal: Early in Tianfu the emperor spoke secretly to Han Wo: "Lu Yi and Pei Zan—which is more loyal to me?"
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianfu era, the emperor spoke privately to Han Wo and asked, "Between Lu Yi and Pei Zan, which of them is more loyal to me?"

sentences.zh: 」偓曰：「扆等皆宰相，安有它腸？

translations.literal: " Wo said: "Yi and the others are all chancellors—how could they have other designs?"
translations.idiomatic: " Wo replied, "Yi and the others are all chancellors. How could they harbor any other intent?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「外言扆不喜我復位，元日易服奔啟夏門，信不？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Outside they say Yi was displeased with my restoration. On New Year's Day he changed clothes and fled to Qixia Gate—is that true?"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "People outside the court say that Yi was displeased with my restoration. On New Year's Day he changed his clothes and fled toward Qixia Gate—is that true?"

sentences.zh: 」偓曰：「孰為陛下言此？

translations.literal: " Wo said: "Who told Your Majesty this?"
translations.idiomatic: " Wo asked, "Who told Your Majesty this?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「崔胤、令狐渙。

translations.literal: " He said: "Cui Yin and Linghu Huan."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor answered, "Cui Yin and Linghu Huan."

sentences.zh: 」偓曰：「設扆如是，亦不足責。

translations.literal: " Wo said: "Even if Yi were so, he would not deserve blame."
translations.idiomatic: " Wo said, "Even if Yi had done as alleged, he would not deserve blame."

sentences.zh: 且陛下反正，扆素不知謀，忽聞兵起，欲出奔耳。

translations.literal: Moreover when Your Majesty restored the throne, Yi never knew of the plot. Suddenly hearing troops rise, he wished only to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when Your Majesty restored the throne, Yi had known nothing of the plot. When he suddenly heard that fighting had broken out, he simply wished to flee.

sentences.zh: 陛下責其不死難則可，以為不喜，乃讒言也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty may blame him for not dying with the hardship, but to say he was displeased is slander.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty may blame him for not sharing the peril of the moment, but to say that he was displeased with your restoration is nothing but slander.

sentences.zh: 」帝遂悟。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon understood.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor thereupon understood.

sentences.zh: 累兼戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly appointed concurrent Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly appointed to serve concurrently as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 帝至自鳳翔，大赦天下，諸道皆賜詔，獨不及李茂貞。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned from Fengxiang he declared a great amnesty for all under heaven; every circuit received an edict except Li Maozhen.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned from Fengxiang, he proclaimed a general amnesty for the empire. Every circuit received an edict except Li Maozhen.

sentences.zh: 扆曰：「國西，鳳翔為最近，跡其罪固不可赦。

translations.literal: Yi said: "West of the state, Fengxiang is nearest. Tracing his crimes he indeed cannot be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "To the west of the realm, Fengxiang is the nearest of the circuits. Judging by his crimes, he indeed cannot be pardoned."

sentences.zh: 然尚修職貢，朝廷未之絕，無宜於詔書有以異也。

translations.literal: Yet he still sends tribute and the court has not cut him off; it is not fitting that the edict treat him differently.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he still sends his regular tribute, and the court has not severed relations with him. The amnesty edict ought not to treat him differently.

sentences.zh: 」始，崔胤罷相，扆代之。

translations.literal: " At first when Cui Yin was removed from the chancellorship, Yi replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier, when Cui Yin was removed from the chancellorship, Yi had replaced him.

sentences.zh: 胤內怨望，及是議以為陰有黨附，貶沂王傅，分司東都。

translations.literal: Yin harbored resentment within, and on this occasion the discussion held that Yi secretly had factional ties; he was demoted to Tutor of the Prince of Yi and assigned to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yin harbored resentment within, and on this occasion the court concluded that Yi had secretly maintained factional ties. Yi was demoted to Tutor of the Prince of Yi and assigned to the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 胤死，復授吏部尚書，從遷洛。

translations.literal: When Yin died, Yi was again appointed Minister of Personnel and followed the move to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Yin died, Yi was again appointed Minister of Personnel and accompanied the court in its move to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 柳璨始附朱全忠，謀去朝廷衣冠有望者，貶扆濮州司戶參軍，殺之白馬驛，年五十九。

translations.literal: Liu Can at first attached himself to Zhu Quanzhong and plotted to remove from court the gentry with standing; Yi was demoted to Registrar of Pu Prefecture and killed at Baima Post Station at age fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can, who had attached himself to Zhu Quanzhong, plotted to remove from court every man of standing in official dress. Yi was demoted to registrar of Pu Prefecture and then killed at Baima Post Station. He was fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 扆初名允迪，後改雲。

translations.literal: Yi's original name was Yundi; later he changed it to Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's original name was Yundi; he later changed it to Yun.

sentences.zh: 鄭綮，字蘊武。

translations.literal: Zheng Qi, style name Yunwu.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Qi, whose courtesy name was Yunwu.

sentences.zh: 及進士第，歷監察御史，擢累左司郎中。

translations.literal: After passing the jinshi examination he served as remonstrating censor and rose through Left Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he served as a remonstrating censor and rose step by step to Director of the Left Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 因窶甚，丐補廬州刺史。

translations.literal: Because he was extremely poor he begged to be supplemented as prefect of Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was desperately poor, he begged to be appointed prefect of Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 黃巢掠淮南，綮移檄請無犯州境，巢笑，為斂兵，州獨完。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao plundered Huainan, Qi sent a proclamation asking that the prefecture not be violated; Chao laughed but restrained his troops, and the prefecture alone remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao ravaged Huainan, Qi sent out a proclamation asking that his prefecture be left untouched. Chao laughed, but he restrained his troops, and Lu Prefecture alone remained intact.

sentences.zh: 僖宗嘉之，賜緋魚。

translations.literal: Xizong commended this and granted crimson fish insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong commended this act and granted him the crimson robe and fish insignia.

sentences.zh: 歲滿去，贏錢千緡藏州庫。

translations.literal: When his term ended he left, having earned a thousand strings of cash stored in the prefectural treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he departed, leaving a surplus of a thousand strings of cash stored in the prefectural treasury.

sentences.zh: 後它盜至，終不犯鄭使君錢。

translations.literal: Later when other bandits came they never touched Prefect Zheng's money.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when other bandits arrived, they never touched the money left by Prefect Zheng.

sentences.zh: 及楊行密為刺史，送都還綮。

translations.literal: When Yang Xingmi became prefect he sent it to the capital and returned it to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xingmi became prefect, he sent the money to the capital and returned it to Qi.

sentences.zh: 王徽為御史大夫，以兵部郎中表知雜事，遷給事中。

translations.literal: Wang Hui as censor-in-chief listed him as Military Department Director handling miscellaneous matters, then promoted to Drafting Middle Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Hui served as censor-in-chief, he appointed Qi Military Department director in charge of miscellaneous matters, and Qi was later promoted to drafting attendant.

sentences.zh: 杜弘徽任中書舍人，綮以其兄讓能輔政，不宜處禁要，上還制書，不報，輒移病去。

translations.literal: Du Hongwei held the post of Secretariat Drafter; Qi because his elder brother Rangneng aided government should not hold a crucial inner post, returned the edict upward; no response came and he immediately claimed illness and left.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Hongwei was appointed Secretariat drafter, Qi argued that because Hongwei's elder brother Rangneng was assisting in government, he ought not hold so sensitive an inner-court post. Qi returned the appointment edict to the throne, and when no answer came, he promptly claimed illness and resigned.

sentences.zh: 召為右散騎常侍，往往條摘失政，眾讙傳之，宰相怒，改國子祭酒，議者不直，復還常侍。

translations.literal: Summoned as Right Regular Cavalier Attendant, he often singled out governmental failures; the crowd spread word of it, the chancellor was angry, changed him to Rector of the Imperial University; critics did not uphold this and he was restored to Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Right Regular Cavalier Attendant and often singled out failures in government for criticism. Word of this spread widely, and the chancellor grew angry and reassigned him as rector of the Imperial University. Critics did not regard this as justified, and he was restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 大順後，王政微，綮每以詩謠托諷，中人有誦之天子前者。

translations.literal: After Datun royal administration grew weak; Qi often used songs and ballads with indirect satire; palace insiders who recited them before the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: After the Datun era, royal administration grew weak. Qi often used songs and ballads to offer veiled criticism, and palace eunuchs would recite them before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 昭宗意其有所蘊未盡，因有司上班簿，遂署其側曰：「可禮部侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Zhaozong thought he had something not yet fully expressed; thereupon the relevant office presented the shift roster and he wrote at the side: "May serve as Vice Minister of Rites and Co-Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong suspected that Qi had more to offer than he had yet shown. When the relevant office presented the roster of officials on duty, the emperor wrote beside Qi's name, "May serve as Vice Minister of Rites and Co-Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery."

sentences.zh: 」綮本善詩，其語多俳諧，故使落調，世共號「鄭五歇後體」。

translations.literal: " Qi was originally skilled at poetry; his language was largely humorous; therefore he made off-key verses; the age together called it "Fifth-of-the-Zheng trailing-rhyme style."
translations.idiomatic: " Qi had long been skilled at poetry, and his language was often humorous and offbeat. For this reason his verses frequently ended with an unexpected trailing rhyme, and the age together called his style "Fifth Zheng's trailing-rhyme verse."

sentences.zh: 至是，省史走其家上謁，綮笑曰：「諸君誤矣，人皆不識字，宰相亦不及我。

translations.literal: At this time provincial clerks ran to his house to pay respects; Qi laughed and said: "You gentlemen are mistaken—people all cannot read, and the chancellor is not my match either."
translations.idiomatic: At this point the provincial clerks hurried to his house to pay their respects. Qi laughed and said, "You gentlemen are mistaken. The people cannot even read, and the chancellor is no match for me either."

sentences.zh: 」史言不妄。

translations.literal: " The clerks said it was no falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: " The clerks insisted that this was no jest.

sentences.zh: 俄聞制詔下，嘆曰：「萬一然，笑殺天下人！

translations.literal: Soon hearing the edict of appointment descend, he sighed: "If by any chance it is so, it will make the world die laughing!"
translations.idiomatic: Before long he heard that the appointment edict had been issued. He sighed and said, "If by any chance this is real, it will make the whole world die laughing!"

sentences.zh: 」既視事，宗戚詣慶，搔首曰：「歇後鄭五作宰相，事可知矣。

translations.literal: " Once he took office, clan kin came to congratulate; he scratched his head and said: "Trailing-rhyme Fifth Zheng made chancellor—the affair can be known."
translations.idiomatic: " Once he assumed office, his clansmen came to congratulate him. He scratched his head and said, "If trailing-rhyme Fifth Zheng has become chancellor, the state of affairs can already be guessed."

sentences.zh: 」固讓，不聽。

translations.literal: " He firmly declined but was not heard.
translations.idiomatic: " He firmly declined the post, but his plea was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 立朝偘然，無復故態。

translations.literal: Standing at court he was stern and proper, no longer his old manner.
translations.idiomatic: In court he conducted himself with grave propriety and showed none of his former manner.

sentences.zh: 自以不為人所瞻望，才三月，以疾乞骸，拜太子少保致仕，卒。

translations.literal: Himself thinking people did not look up to him, in only three months citing illness he begged bones and was made Crown Prince Junior Tutor with retirement; he died.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling that people did not look up to him, after only three months he cited illness and requested retirement. He was appointed Crown Prince Junior Tutor with permission to retire, and soon died.

sentences.zh: 朱朴，襄州襄陽人。

translations.literal: Zhu Pu, a man of Xiangyang in Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Pu was a native of Xiangyang in Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以三史舉，繇荊門令進京兆府司錄參軍，改著作郎。

translations.literal: Recommended through the Three Histories examination, from Jingmen magistrate he advanced to Metropolitan Assistant Recorder, then changed to Drafting Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service through the Three Histories examination, rose from magistrate of Jingmen to assistant recorder of the metropolitan prefecture, and was later appointed drafting gentleman.

sentences.zh: 乾寧初，太府少卿李元實欲取中外九品以上官兩月俸助軍興，朴上疏執不可而止。

translations.literal: Early in Qianning Junior Chamberlain of the Grand Storehouse Li Yuanshi wished to take two months' salary from officials of the ninth rank and above inside and outside to aid military expansion; Pu memorialized firmly against and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianning era, Li Yuanshi, Junior Chamberlain of the Grand Storehouse, proposed seizing two months' salary from every official of the ninth rank and above, inside and outside the capital, to fund the armies. Pu submitted a memorial firmly opposing the plan, and the proposal was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 擢國子《毛詩》博士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Doctor of the Mao Odes in the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Doctor of the Mao Odes at the National University.

sentences.zh: 上書言當世事，議遷都曰：「古王者不常厥居，皆觀天地興衰，隨時制事。

translations.literal: He memorialized on current affairs, discussing moving the capital: "Ancient kings did not fix their residence; all observed heaven and earth's rise and fall and made policy according to the time."
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial on current affairs and discussed moving the capital, writing, "Ancient kings did not keep to a single residence. They all observed the rise and fall of heaven and earth and shaped policy according to the times."

sentences.zh: 關中，隋家所都，我實因之，凡三百歲，文物資貨，奢侈僭偽皆極焉。

translations.literal: Guanzhong was the Sui capital—we took it over; altogether three hundred years; cultural objects, goods and wealth, luxury and usurpation all reached their extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong was the capital of the Sui, and we in turn took it over. For three hundred years cultural treasures, goods, luxury, and usurpation all reached their extreme there.

sentences.zh: 廣明巨盜陷覆宮闕，局署帑藏，裏闬井肆，所存十二，比幸石門、華陰，十二之中又亡八九，高祖、太宗之制蕩然矣。

translations.literal: In Guangming the great bandit overthrew and buried the palace; bureau offices, treasury stores, lanes and markets—twelve parts remained. Compared with the flight to Shimen and Huayin, of the twelve eight or nine more were lost; the institutions of Gaozu and Taizong were swept away.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangming era the great rebel overran and destroyed the palace. Of the government offices, treasuries, lanes, and markets, only a tenth remained. After the emperor's flight to Shimen and Huayin, eight or nine tenths of even that remnant were lost. The institutions established by Gaozu and Taizong were swept away.

sentences.zh: 夫襄、鄧之西，夷溫數百里，其東，漢輿、鳳林為之關，南，菊潭環屈而流屬於漢，西有上洛重山之險，北有白崖聯絡，乃形勝之地，沃衍之墟。

translations.literal: West of Xiang and Deng several hundred li of Yi warmth; east the Han chariot and Fenglin as its passes; south Jutan bends and flows into the Han; west the dangerous heights of Shangluo mountains; north Bais precipice linked—terrain advantageous, fertile fields.
translations.idiomatic: West of Xiang and Deng lie several hundred li of warm frontier lands. To the east, Han Yu and Fenglin form its passes. To the south, Jutan bends and flows into the Han River. To the west stand the steep mountains of Shangluo. To the north, white cliffs link together. It is a place of strategic advantage and fertile ground.

sentences.zh: 若廣浚漕渠，運天下之財，可使大集。

translations.literal: If widely dredging the transport canal, moving the empire's wealth, great collection can be made.
translations.idiomatic: If the transport canals were broadly dredged and the wealth of the empire moved there, great resources could be gathered.

sentences.zh: 自古中興之君，去已衰之衰，就未王而王。

translations.literal: From antiquity restoring-the-dynasty rulers leave the already declining and go to the not yet kingship.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity, rulers who restored a dynasty have left what was already in decline and gone to a place not yet crowned with kingship.

sentences.zh: 今南陽，漢光武雖起而未王也。

translations.literal: Now Nanyang—Han Guangwu though risen was not yet king.
translations.idiomatic: Nanyang today is like the place where Emperor Guangwu of Han rose to power before he had yet become king.

sentences.zh: 臣視山河壯麗處多，故都已盛而衰，難可興已；

translations.literal: Your servant views many places where mountains and rivers are majestic; therefore the old capital flourished then declined, hard to revive;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has observed that majestic mountains and rivers are abundant elsewhere, while the old capital has already flourished and declined and can hardly be revived again;

sentences.zh: 江南土薄水淺，人心囂浮輕巧，不可以都；

translations.literal: South of the Yangtze soil thin water shallow, people's hearts noisy floating and clever—cannot be capital;
translations.idiomatic: south of the Yangtze the soil is thin and the waters shallow, and the people's hearts are restless, frivolous, and clever—it cannot serve as a capital;

sentences.zh: 河北土厚水深，人心強愎狠戾，不可以都。

translations.literal: Hebei soil thick water deep, people's hearts strong obstinate fierce cruel—cannot be capital.
translations.idiomatic: north of the Yellow River the soil is thick and the waters deep, but the people's hearts are stubborn, fierce, and cruel—it too cannot serve as a capital.

sentences.zh: 惟襄、鄧實惟中原，人心質良，去秦咫尺，而有上洛為之限，永無夷狄侵軼之虞，此建都之極選也。

translations.literal: Only Xiang and Deng are truly central plains; people's hearts plain and good; close to Qin by a foot and Shangluo as its limit—forever no barbarian invasion worry—this is the extreme choice for establishing capital.
translations.idiomatic: Only Xiang and Deng are truly the central plains. The people there are plain and good-hearted. They lie within a stone's throw of Qin, yet Shangluo forms a natural barrier, so there would forever be no fear of barbarian raids. This is the finest possible choice for establishing the capital.

sentences.zh: 」不報。

translations.literal: " There was no response.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne gave no reply.

sentences.zh: 朴為人木強，無它能。

translations.literal: Pu was dull by nature and had no other ability.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was dull and inflexible by nature and possessed no other special talent.

sentences.zh: 方是時，天子失政，思用特起士，任之以中興，而朴所善方士許巖士得幸，出入禁中，言朴有經濟才，又水部郎中何迎亦表其賢，帝召與語，擢左諫議大夫、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven lost government, thinking to use specially raised scholars to entrust restoration; what Pu was good at was the alchemist Xu Yanshi favored, entering and leaving the forbidden interior, saying Pu had economic talent; also Water Department Director He Ying memorialized his worth; the emperor summoned to converse; promoted Left Remonstrating Grandee and Co-Director.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor had lost control of government and wished to raise unusual men from obscurity and entrust them with restoring the dynasty. The alchemist Xu Yanshi, whom Pu favored, won favor and moved in and out of the inner palace, saying that Pu possessed talent for statecraft. He Ying, director of the Water Department, also memorialized Pu's worth. The emperor summoned Pu for an audience and promoted him to Left Remonstrating Grandee and Co-Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 以素無聞，人人大驚，俄判戶部，進中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Never heard of before—everyone greatly astonished; soon presiding Revenue Ministry, advanced Secretariat Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had previously been unknown, everyone was greatly astonished. Before long he was put in charge of the Revenue Ministry and then promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 帝益治兵，所處可一委朴。

translations.literal: The emperor increasingly managed troops; what was done could all be entrusted to Pu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor increasingly devoted himself to military affairs, and nearly everything that was done could be entrusted to Pu.

sentences.zh: 朴移檄四方，令近者出甲士，資饋饟，遠者以羨余上。

translations.literal: Pu moved proclamations to the four quarters ordering the near to send armored soldiers, provisions and rations, the far to submit surplus tribute upward.
translations.idiomatic: Pu issued proclamations to the four quarters, ordering nearby regions to send armored troops and supplies and distant regions to submit their surplus revenues to the throne.

sentences.zh: 後數月，巖士為韓建所殺，朴罷為秘書監，三貶郴州司戶參軍，卒。

translations.literal: Several months later Yanshi was killed by Han Jian; Pu removed to Secretary Supervisor; three demotions to Chen Prefecture Registrar; died.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later Yanshi was killed by Han Jian. Pu was removed to Secretary Supervisor, then demoted three times to registrar of Chen Prefecture, and died.

sentences.zh: 與朴皆相者孫偓。

translations.literal: Together with Pu as chancellor was Sun Wo.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as chancellor together with Pu was Sun Wo.

sentences.zh: 孫偓，字龍光。

translations.literal: Sun Wo, style name Longguang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Wo, whose courtesy name was Longguang.

sentences.zh: 父景商，為天平軍節度使。

translations.literal: His father Jingshang was Tianping military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sun Jingshang served as military commissioner of Tianping.

sentences.zh: 偓第進士，歷顯官，以戶部侍郎同中書門下平章事，遷門下，為鳳翔四面行營都統。

translations.literal: Wo second in jinshi, passed through eminent offices; as Revenue Vice Minister Co-Director; moved to Chancellery; made overall commander of Fengxiang four-sided campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Wo placed second in the jinshi examination and rose through eminent offices. He became Co-Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery while serving as Vice Minister of Revenue, was transferred to the Chancellery, and was appointed overall commander of the four-sided campaign against Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 俄兼禮部尚書、行營節度諸軍都統招討處置等使。

translations.literal: Soon also Minister of Rites, campaign commissioner overall command pacify dispose etc.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he also held the concurrent posts of Minister of Rites and commissioner for pacification, disposal, and overall command of the campaign armies.

sentences.zh: 始，家第堂柱生槐枝，期而茂，既而偓秉政，封樂安縣侯。

translations.literal: At first at the family hall pillars sophora branches grew; in due time flourished; then Wo held government; enfeoffed Marquis of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, sophora branches had sprouted from a pillar in the hall of his family residence and flourished in due season. Soon afterward Wo took power and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Le'an.

sentences.zh: 與朴皆貶衡州司馬，卒。

translations.literal: Together with Pu both demoted Hengzhou Militia Vice-Prefect; died.
translations.idiomatic: Like Pu, he was demoted to militia vice-prefect of Heng Prefecture and died.

sentences.zh: 偓性通簡，不矯飭，嘗曰：「士茍有行，不必以己長形彼短、己清彰彼濁。

translations.literal: Wo's nature was open and simple, not putting on airs; once said: "If a gentleman has conduct, he need not use his length to expose others' shortness, his clarity to display others' turbidity."
translations.idiomatic: Wo was open and unpretentious by nature and did not put on airs. He once said, "If a gentleman truly possesses moral conduct, he need not use his own strengths to expose others' weaknesses or his own purity to highlight others' corruption."

sentences.zh: 」每對客，奴童相詬曳仆諸前，不之責，曰：「若持怒心，即自撓矣。」

translations.literal: " Whenever receiving guests, servant boys would revile and drag each other before him without his blaming; he said: "If you hold anger in your heart, you will defeat yourself."
translations.idiomatic: " Whenever he received guests, his servant boys would curse and wrestle with one another in front of him, yet he never blamed them. He said, "If you harbor anger in your heart, you defeat yourself."

sentences.zh: 兄儲，歷天雄節度使，終兵部尚書。

translations.literal: His elder brother Chu passed through Tianxiong commissioner and ended as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Sun Chu served as military commissioner of Tianxiong and ended his career as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 韓偓，字致光，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Han Wo, style name Zhiguang, a man of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wo, whose courtesy name was Zhiguang, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，佐河中幕府。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and aided the Hedong staff.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served on the staff of the Hedong command.

sentences.zh: 召拜左拾遺，以疾解。

translations.literal: Summoned as Left Remonstrator, resigned for illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed Left Remonstrator, but resigned because of illness.

sentences.zh: 後遷累左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Later repeatedly promoted to Left Remonstrating Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted step by step to Left Remonstrating Grandee.

sentences.zh: 宰相崔胤判度支，表以自副。

translations.literal: Chancellor Cui Yin presiding over the budget listed him as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Chancellor Cui Yin took charge of the budget, he recommended Wo as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 王溥薦為翰林學士，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: Wang Pu recommended him as Hanlin academician; promoted Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pu recommended him for the Hanlin Academy, and he was later promoted to Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 偓嘗與胤定策誅劉季述，昭宗反正，為功臣。

translations.literal: Wo once with Yin settled policy to execute Liu Jishu; Zhaozong restored the throne; became a merit minister.
translations.idiomatic: Wo once joined with Yin in planning the execution of Liu Jishu. When Emperor Zhaozong restored the throne, Wo was counted among the meritorious ministers.

sentences.zh: 帝疾宦人驕橫，欲盡去之。

translations.literal: The emperor detested eunuchs' arrogance and wished to remove all of them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor resented the eunuchs' arrogance and wished to remove them all.

sentences.zh: 偓曰：「陛下誅季述時，余皆赦不問，今又誅之，誰不懼死？

translations.literal: Wo said: "When Your Majesty executed Jishu, the rest were all pardoned without inquiry; now if you execute again, who will not fear death?"
translations.idiomatic: Wo said, "When Your Majesty executed Jishu, all the others were pardoned and left unpunished. If you execute eunuchs again now, who will not fear for his life?"

sentences.zh: 含垢隱忍，須後可也。

translations.literal: Bearing filth and hiding resentment must wait for later.
translations.idiomatic: You must bear what is foul and endure in patience until a later time.

sentences.zh: 天子威柄，今散在方面，若上下同心，攝領權綱，猶冀天下可治。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's authority is now scattered among the regions; if above and below share one heart and gather the power framework, still may hope the empire can be governed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's authority is now scattered among the regional commanders. If court and provinces can act with one heart and gather power back into a single framework, there may still be hope of governing the realm.

sentences.zh: 宦人忠厚可任者，假以恩幸，使自翦其黨，蔑有不濟。

translations.literal: Eunuchs who are loyal and thick and can be employed—lend them favor and grace, have them cut their own faction—there will be nothing not successful.
translations.idiomatic: Among the eunuchs there are men loyal and dependable enough to be used. Grant them favor and have them cut down their own factions, and nothing will fail to succeed.

sentences.zh: 今食度支者乃八千人，公私牽屬不減二萬，雖誅六七巨魁，未見有益，適固其逆心耳。

translations.literal: Now those eating the revenue bureau are eight thousand; public and private connections no less than twenty thousand—though executing six or seven great chiefs, no benefit seen, only solidifying their rebellious hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Today eight thousand men draw salaries from the revenue directorate, and their public and private dependents number no fewer than twenty thousand. Even if six or seven great leaders were executed, no real benefit would be seen; it would only harden their rebellious resolve.

sentences.zh: 」帝前膝曰：「此一事終始屬卿。」

translations.literal: " The emperor leaned forward and said: "This one affair from start to finish belongs to you."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor leaned forward and said, "From beginning to end, this whole affair is entrusted to you."

sentences.zh: 中書舍人令狐渙任機巧，帝嘗欲以當國，俄又悔曰：「渙作宰相或誤國，朕當先用卿。

translations.literal: Secretariat Drafter Linghu Huan was skilled in schemes; the emperor once wished to make him hold government; soon again regretted: "Huan as chancellor might ruin the state—I should first use you."
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat drafter Linghu Huan was skilled in intrigue. The emperor once wished to put him in charge of government, but soon regretted it and said, "If Huan becomes chancellor he may ruin the state. I ought to use you first."

sentences.zh: 」辭曰：「渙再世宰相，練故事，陛下業已許之。

translations.literal: " Wo declined: "Huan is a twice-generation chancellor, skilled in precedents; Your Majesty already promised him."
translations.idiomatic: " Wo declined, saying, "Huan comes from two generations of chancellors and is thoroughly versed in precedent. Your Majesty has already promised him the post."

sentences.zh: 若許渙可改，許臣獨不可移乎？

translations.literal: If permitting Huan can be changed, permitting your servant alone cannot be moved?
translations.idiomatic: If a promise to Huan may be changed, may a promise to me alone not be changed as well?

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「我未嘗面命，亦何憚？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "I never commanded face to face—what is there to fear?"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "I never gave him the appointment in person. What is there to fear?"

sentences.zh: 」偓因薦御史大夫趙崇勁正雅重，可以準繩中外。

translations.literal: " Wo thereby recommended Censor-in-Chief Zhao Chong upright, elegant, and weighty, able to be the standard inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: " Wo then recommended Censor-in-Chief Zhao Chong, a man of stern integrity and weighty character who could serve as a standard for the court and the realm.

sentences.zh: 帝知偓，崇門生也，嘆其能讓。

translations.literal: The emperor knew Wo was Chong's student and sighed at his ability to yield.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew that Wo had been Zhao Chong's student and marveled at his willingness to yield.

sentences.zh: 初，李繼昭等以功皆進同中書門下平章事，時謂「三使相」，後稍稍更附韓全誨、周敬容，皆忌胤。

translations.literal: At first Li Jizhao and others for merit all advanced Co-Director; the time called "three commissioner-chancellors"; later gradually more attached to Han Quanhui and Zhou Jingrong—all resented Yin.
translations.idiomatic: At first Li Jizhao and the others were all promoted to Co-Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery for their merits, and the age called them the "Three Commissioner-Chancellors." Later they gradually attached themselves to Han Quanhui and Zhou Jingrong, and all came to resent Cui Yin.

sentences.zh: 胤聞，召鳳翔李茂貞入朝，使留族子繼筠宿衛。

translations.literal: Yin heard and summoned Fengxiang Li Maozhen to court, had his clan nephew Jiyun remain as inner guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin heard of this, he summoned Li Maozhen of Fengxiang to court and had Maozhen's clansman Li Jiyun remain behind as an inner guard.

sentences.zh: 偓聞，以為不可，胤不納。

translations.literal: Wo heard, thought it impossible; Yin did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When Wo heard of this, he regarded the plan as unwise, but Yin would not listen.

sentences.zh: 偓又語令狐渙，渙曰：「吾屬不惜宰相邪？

translations.literal: Wo again spoke to Linghu Huan; Huan said: "Our sort does not cherish the chancellorship?"
translations.idiomatic: Wo spoke again to Linghu Huan. Huan said, "Do you think men like us do not value the chancellorship?"

sentences.zh: 無衛軍則為閹豎所圖矣。

translations.literal: Without guard troops we will be schemed against by the eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: Without guard troops we shall be plotted against by the eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 」偓曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Wo said: "Not so."
translations.idiomatic: " Wo said, "That is not so."

sentences.zh: 無兵則家與國安，有兵則家與國不可保。

translations.literal: Without troops then family and state are secure; with troops then family and state cannot be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Without troops, both family and state may be secure; with troops, neither family nor state can be preserved.

sentences.zh: 」胤聞，憂，未知所出。

translations.literal: " When Yin heard he was worried and did not know what course to take.
translations.idiomatic: " When Yin heard this, he grew anxious and did not know what to do.

sentences.zh: 李彥弼見帝倨甚，帝不平，偓請逐之，赦其黨許自新，則狂謀自破，帝不用。

translations.literal: Li Yanbi when seeing the emperor was very arrogant; the emperor was displeased; Wo asked to expel him, pardon his faction allowing renewal, then mad plots would break themselves; the emperor did not use this.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanbi behaved with great arrogance when he met the emperor, and the emperor was displeased. Wo asked that Yanbi be expelled and his followers pardoned on condition of reform, saying that their reckless plots would then collapse of themselves, but the emperor did not adopt the plan.

sentences.zh: 彥弼譖偓及渙漏禁省語，不可與圖政，帝怒，曰：「卿有官屬，日夕議事，奈何不欲我見學士邪？

translations.literal: Yanbi slandered Wo and Huan for leaking forbidden-palace speech, unfit to plan government; the emperor was angry and said: "You have official subordinates discussing affairs day and night—why do you not wish me to see the academicians?"
translations.idiomatic: Yanbi slandered Wo and Huan for leaking inner-court secrets and said they were unfit to take part in governing. The emperor grew angry and said, "You have your own officials discussing affairs day and night—why do you not wish me to see the academicians?"

sentences.zh: 」繼昭等飲殿中自如，帝怒，偓曰：「三使相有功，不如厚與金帛官爵，毋使豫政事。

translations.literal: " Jizhao and others drank in the hall as they pleased; the emperor was angry; Wo said: "The three commissioner-chancellors have merit—better to give them generously gold, silk, offices and ranks, and not let them participate in government affairs."
translations.idiomatic: " Jizhao and the others drank freely in the hall as though it were their own house, and the emperor was furious. Wo said, "The Three Commissioner-Chancellors have rendered service. It would be better to reward them generously with gold, silk, offices, and titles, and not allow them to take part in government affairs."

sentences.zh: 今宰相不得顓決事，繼昭輩所奏必聽。

translations.literal: Now the chancellor cannot exclusively decide affairs; whatever Jizhao's crowd memorializes must be heard.
translations.idiomatic: At present the chancellor cannot decide affairs on his own, and whatever Jizhao and his associates submit must be heard.

sentences.zh: 它日遽改，則人人生怨。

translations.literal: If one day it is suddenly changed, then everyone will harbor resentment.
translations.idiomatic: If policy is suddenly changed another day, everyone will harbor resentment.

sentences.zh: 初以衛兵檢中人，今敕使、衛兵為一，臣竊寒心，願詔茂貞還其衛軍。

translations.literal: At first guards inspected the inner attendants; now edict-envoys and guards are one—I privately feel chilled in heart and wish to edict Maozhen to return his guard army.
translations.idiomatic: At first the guard troops were used to keep watch over the inner attendants. Now the edict-envoys and the guards have become one body, and I am privately filled with dread. I beg that an edict be issued ordering Maozhen to withdraw his guard troops.

sentences.zh: 不然，兩鎮兵鬥闕下，朝廷危矣。

translations.literal: Otherwise the two commands' troops will fight below the palace gates and the court will be in peril.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the armies of the two commands will fight beneath the palace gates, and the court will be in grave peril.

sentences.zh: 」及胤召朱全忠討全誨，汴兵將至，偓勸胤督茂貞還衛卒。

translations.literal: " When Yin summoned Zhu Quanzhong to attack Quanhui, Bian troops were about to arrive; Wo urged Yin to press Maozhen to return the guard soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: " When Yin summoned Zhu Quanzhong to attack Quanhui and the Bian armies were about to arrive, Wo urged Yin to press Maozhen to withdraw his guard troops.

sentences.zh: 又勸表暴內臣罪，因誅全誨等；

translations.literal: He also urged a memorial exposing the inner attendants' crimes and thereby executing Quanhui and others;
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that a memorial be submitted exposing the crimes of the inner attendants so that Quanhui and the others might be executed;

sentences.zh: 若茂貞不如詔，即許全忠入朝。

translations.literal: if Maozhen did not follow the edict, then permit Quanzhong to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: and if Maozhen did not obey the edict, then Quanzhong should be permitted to enter the capital.

sentences.zh: 未及用，而全誨等已劫帝西幸。

translations.literal: Before this could be used, Quanhui and others had already seized the emperor on a western flight.
translations.idiomatic: Before these plans could be carried out, Quanhui and the others had already seized the emperor and forced him west on campaign.

sentences.zh: 偓夜追及鄠，見帝慟哭。

translations.literal: Wo by night overtook him at E and on seeing the emperor wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Wo overtook the emperor by night at E Prefecture and wept bitterly when he saw him.

sentences.zh: 至鳳翔，遷兵部侍郎，進承旨。

translations.literal: Reaching Fengxiang he was moved to Vice Minister of War and advanced to chief academician.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Fengxiang, he was appointed Vice Minister of War and then promoted to chief academician of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 宰相韋貽範母喪，詔還位，偓當草制，上言：「貽範處喪未數月，遽使視事，傷孝子心。

translations.literal: Chancellor Wei Yifan had his mother's mourning; an edict restored him to office; Wo was to draft the edict and memorialized: "Yifan is in mourning not yet several months—hastily making him attend to affairs wounds a filial son's heart."
translations.idiomatic: When Chancellor Wei Yifan was in mourning for his mother, an edict ordered him back to office. Wo was to draft the appointment edict and memorialized, "Yifan has been in mourning only a few months. To hurry him back to office wounds the heart of a filial son."

sentences.zh: 今中書事，一相可辦。

translations.literal: Now Secretariat-Chancellery affairs—one chancellor can handle them.
translations.idiomatic: At present the affairs of the Secretariat-Chancellery can be handled by a single chancellor.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠惜貽範才，俟變缞而召可也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly cherishes Yifan's talent, wait until he changes from hemp mourning and then summon him.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly values Yifan's talent, you may summon him after he has completed the period of hemp mourning.

sentences.zh: 何必使出峨冠廟堂，入泣血柩側，毀瘠則廢務，勤恪則忘哀，此非人情可處也。

translations.literal: Why must you make him go out with lofty cap in the temple hall and enter weeping blood beside the coffin—if emaciated then duties are abandoned, if diligent then grief is forgotten—this is not a situation human feeling can bear.
translations.idiomatic: Why must you send him forth in court dress to the temple hall and then have him stand weeping beside the coffin? If he grows emaciated, state affairs are neglected; if he remains diligent, he forgets his grief. This is not a situation any human heart can bear.

sentences.zh: 」學士使馬從皓逼偓求草，偓曰：「腕可斷，麻不可草！

translations.literal: " The academician envoy Ma Conghao pressed Wo to draft; Wo said: "The wrist may be severed—the hemp edict may not be drafted!"
translations.idiomatic: " The academician's envoy Ma Conghao pressed Wo to draft the edict. Wo said, "My wrist may be cut off, but I will not draft this edict!"

sentences.zh: 」從皓曰：「君求死邪？

translations.literal: " Conghao said: "Sir, do you seek death?"
translations.idiomatic: " Conghao said, "Do you seek death, sir?"

sentences.zh: 」偓曰：「吾職內署，可默默乎？

translations.literal: " Wo said: "My duty is the inner secretariat—can I remain silent?"
translations.idiomatic: " Wo said, "My duty lies in the inner secretariat. How can I remain silent?"

sentences.zh: 」明日，百官至，而麻不出，宦侍合噪。

translations.literal: " The next day the hundred officials arrived but the hemp edict did not appear; palace attendants all clamored together.
translations.idiomatic: " The next day the officials all arrived, but the edict did not appear, and the palace attendants raised a great clamor together.

sentences.zh: 茂貞入見帝曰：「命宰相而學士不草麻，非反邪？

translations.literal: Maozhen entered to see the emperor and said: "An appointment of chancellor yet the academician will not draft hemp—is this not rebellion?"
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen entered to see the emperor and said, "A chancellor has been appointed, yet the academician refuses to draft the edict—is this not rebellion?"

sentences.zh: 」艴然出。

translations.literal: " He flushed angrily and left.
translations.idiomatic: " He flushed with anger and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 姚洎聞曰：「使我當直，亦繼以死。

translations.literal: Yao Ji hearing said: "If I were on duty, I too would follow with death."
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Ji heard of this, he said, "If I had been on duty, I too would have chosen death rather than comply."

sentences.zh: 」既而帝畏茂貞，卒詔貽範還相，洎代草麻。

translations.literal: " Before long the emperor feared Maozhen and finally edicted Yifan back as chancellor; Ji drafted the hemp edict in his place.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long the emperor, fearing Maozhen, at last issued an edict restoring Yifan to the chancellorship, and Ji drafted the appointment edict in Wo's place.

sentences.zh: 自是宦黨怒偓甚。

translations.literal: From this the eunuch faction was very angry with Wo.
translations.idiomatic: From this time the eunuch faction harbored intense anger toward Wo.

sentences.zh: 從皓讓偓曰：「南司輕北司甚，君乃崔胤、王溥所薦，今日北司雖殺之可也。

translations.literal: Conghao reproached Wo: "The southern offices greatly despise the northern offices. You were recommended by Cui Yin and Wang Pu—today the northern offices could kill you and that would be that."
translations.idiomatic: Conghao reproached Wo, saying, "The southern offices hold the northern offices in great contempt. You were recommended by Cui Yin and Wang Pu. Today the northern offices could kill you without consequence."

sentences.zh: 兩軍樞密，以君周歲無奉入，吾等議救接，君知之乎？

translations.literal: The two armies' secretariat—because you for a full year have had no salary income, we are discussing relief support—do you know this?"
translations.idiomatic: The secretariats of the two armies say that you have received no salary income for a full year, and we are discussing how to provide relief. Do you know this?"

sentences.zh: 」偓不敢對。

translations.literal: " Wo dared not reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Wo dared not answer.

sentences.zh: 茂貞疑帝間出依全忠，以兵衛行在。

translations.literal: Maozhen suspected the emperor might slip out in secret to rely on Quanzhong and used troops to guard the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen suspected that the emperor might secretly slip away to place himself under Quanzhong's protection, and he posted troops to guard the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 帝行武德殿前，因至尚食局，會學士獨在，宮人招偓，偓至，再拜哭曰：「崔胤甚健，全忠軍必濟。
