translations.literal: The emperor walked before Wude Hall and then went to the Food Service Bureau; happening upon the academician alone, palace women summoned Wo; Wo came, bowed twice and wept: "Cui Yin is very vigorous—Quanzhong's army is sure to succeed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was walking before Wude Hall and then went to the Food Service Bureau. Finding the academician alone there, palace women summoned Wo. When Wo arrived he bowed twice and wept, saying, "Cui Yin is in excellent health. Quanzhong's army is sure to prevail."

sentences.zh: 」帝喜，偓曰：「願陛下還宮，無為人知。

translations.literal: " The emperor was pleased; Wo said: "I wish Your Majesty to return to the palace without others knowing."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was delighted. Wo said, "I pray that Your Majesty return to the palace without anyone knowing."

sentences.zh: 」帝賜以面豆而去。

translations.literal: " The emperor gave him noodles and beans and he left.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor gave him noodles and beans, and he departed.

sentences.zh: 全誨誅，宮人多坐死。

translations.literal: When Quanhui was executed many palace women were punished by death.
translations.idiomatic: After Quanhui was executed, many palace women were put to death as well.

sentences.zh: 帝欲盡去餘黨，偓曰：「禮，人臣無將，將必誅，宮婢負恩不可赦。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to remove all the remaining faction; Wo said: "By ritual, if a minister has rebellious intent he must be executed; palace maids who betray grace cannot be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to remove all the remaining faction. Wo said, "By ritual law, when a minister harbors rebellious intent he must be executed, and palace maids who betray their sovereign's grace cannot be pardoned."

sentences.zh: 然不三十年不能成人，盡誅則傷仁。

translations.literal: Yet not in thirty years can one become an adult—executing all would wound benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a person cannot reach adulthood in less than thirty years, and to execute them all would wound the principle of benevolence.

sentences.zh: 願去尤者，自內安外，以靜群心。

translations.literal: I wish to remove the worst offenders; from within secure the without, to quiet all hearts.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that only the worst offenders be removed, so that security within may bring calm without and all hearts may be quieted.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「善。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 」崔胤請以輝王為元帥，帝問偓：「它日累吾兒否？

translations.literal: " Cui Yin asked to make the Prince of Hui commander-in-chief; the emperor asked Wo: "Will it burden my son another day?"
translations.idiomatic: " Cui Yin asked that the Prince of Hui be made commander-in-chief. The emperor asked Wo, "Will this bring trouble upon my son in days to come?"

sentences.zh: 」偓曰：「陛下在東內時，天陰雺，王聞烏聲曰：『上與後幽困，烏雀聲亦悲。

translations.literal: " Wo said: "When Your Majesty was in the eastern inner palace, the sky was dark and misty; the prince hearing crow sounds said: 'The sovereign and empress are confined in gloom—even the crows and sparrows sound mournful.'"
translations.idiomatic: " Wo said, "When Your Majesty was confined in the eastern inner palace, the sky was dark and misty. The prince heard the cry of crows and said, 'The sovereign and empress are confined in gloom—even the cries of crows and sparrows sound mournful.'"

sentences.zh: 』陛下聞之惻然，有是否？

translations.literal: ' Your Majesty hearing this was moved to compassion—is that so or not?"
translations.idiomatic: ' Did Your Majesty not hear this and feel moved to compassion—is that not so?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「然。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "It is so."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "It is so."

sentences.zh: 是兒天生忠孝，與人異。

translations.literal: This son is by nature loyal and filial, different from others.
translations.idiomatic: This son is loyal and filial by nature, unlike other men.

sentences.zh: 」意遂決。

translations.literal: " His mind was thereupon decided.
translations.idiomatic: " His mind was thereupon made up.

sentences.zh: 偓議附胤類如此。

translations.literal: Wo's counsels attached to Yin were mostly of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Wo's counsels in support of Yin were mostly of this kind.

sentences.zh: 帝反正，勵精政事，偓處可機密，率與帝意合，欲相者三四，讓不敢當。

translations.literal: When the emperor restored the throne he applied himself to government; Wo handled what could be secret and mostly matched the emperor's intent; three or four times he was wanted as chancellor but declined and dared not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor restored the throne he devoted himself diligently to government. Wo handled confidential matters and usually agreed with the emperor's intent. Three or four times the emperor wished to make him chancellor, but Wo declined and dared not accept.

sentences.zh: 蘇檢復引同輔政，遂固辭。

translations.literal: Su Jian again drew him to assist in government, and he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Jian again drew him into joint government, he firmly declined once more.

sentences.zh: 初，偓侍宴，與京兆鄭元規、威遠使陳班並席，辭曰：「學士不與外班接。

translations.literal: At first when Wo attended a feast with Metropolitan Zheng Yuangui and Weiyuan envoy Chen Ban at the same mat, he declined: "Academicians do not sit with the outer roster."
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion when Wo was attending a feast seated together with Zheng Yuangui of the metropolitan prefecture and Chen Ban, envoy of Weiyuan, he declined, saying, "Academicians do not sit with the outer roster of officials."

sentences.zh: 」主席者固請，乃坐。

translations.literal: " The host firmly requested and he then sat.
translations.idiomatic: " The host of the feast pressed him firmly, and only then did he sit down.

sentences.zh: 既元規、班至，終絕席。

translations.literal: Once Yuangui and Ban arrived he finally broke off the mat.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuangui and Ban arrived, he at last broke off the shared mat.

sentences.zh: 全忠、胤臨陛宣事，坐者皆去席，偓不動，曰：「侍宴無輒立，二公將以我為知禮。

translations.literal: Quanzhong and Yin came to the steps to announce affairs; those seated all left their mats; Wo did not move and said: "At a feast one does not casually rise—the two lords will take me as knowing ritual."
translations.idiomatic: When Quanzhong and Yin came to the steps to announce affairs, all those seated rose from their mats, but Wo did not move. He said, "At a feast one does not rise casually. The two lords will take me for a man who understands ritual."

sentences.zh: 」全忠怒偓薄己，悻然出。

translations.literal: " Quanzhong was angry that Wo slighted him and left resentfully.
translations.idiomatic: " Quanzhong was angry that Wo had slighted him and withdrew in resentment.

sentences.zh: 有譖偓喜侵侮有位，胤亦與偓貳。

translations.literal: Someone slandered that Wo delighted in insulting those in office; Yin also turned from Wo.
translations.idiomatic: Someone slandered Wo, saying that he delighted in insulting men of rank. Yin also turned away from him.

sentences.zh: 會逐王溥、陸扆，帝以王贊、趙崇為相，胤執贊、崇非宰相器，帝不得已而罷。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Pu and Lu Yi were expelled; the emperor made Wang Zan and Zhao Chong chancellors; Yin insisted Zan and Chong were not chancellor material; the emperor had no choice but to dismiss them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Pu and Lu Yi were driven out. The emperor appointed Wang Zan and Zhao Chong as chancellors, but Yin insisted that neither was fit for the chancellorship, and the emperor had no choice but to dismiss them.

sentences.zh: 贊、崇皆偓所薦為宰相者。

translations.literal: Zan and Chong were both those Wo had recommended as chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Both Zan and Chong were men Wo had recommended for the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 全忠見帝，斥偓罪，帝數顧胤，胤不為解。

translations.literal: Quanzhong saw the emperor and denounced Wo's crimes; the emperor repeatedly looked toward Yin; Yin did not speak in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong saw the emperor and denounced Wo's crimes. The emperor repeatedly looked toward Yin for help, but Yin offered no defense.

sentences.zh: 全忠至中書，欲召偓殺之。

translations.literal: Quanzhong came to the Secretariat and wished to summon Wo and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong went to the Secretariat and wished to summon Wo and have him killed.

sentences.zh: 鄭元規曰：「偓位侍郎、學士承旨，公無遽。

translations.literal: Zheng Yuangui said: "Wo holds the rank of vice minister and chief academician—my lord, do not be hasty."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yuangui said, "Wo holds the rank of vice minister and chief academician of the Hanlin Academy. My lord, you must not act in haste."

sentences.zh: 」全忠乃止，貶濮州司馬。

translations.literal: " Quanzhong then stopped and demoted him to Militia Vice-Prefect of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: " Quanzhong thereupon desisted and demoted Wo to militia vice-prefect of Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 帝執其手流涕曰：「我左右無人矣。

translations.literal: The emperor grasped his hand with tears flowing and said: "I have no one left at my side."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his hand with tears streaming down his face and said, "I have no one left at my side."

sentences.zh: 」再貶榮懿尉，徙鄧州司馬。

translations.literal: " He was again demoted to Defender of Rongyi and moved to Militia Vice-Prefect of Deng.
translations.idiomatic: " He was demoted again to defender of Rongyi and transferred to militia vice-prefect of Deng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天祐二年，復召為學士，還故官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianyou he was again summoned as academician and restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianyou he was again summoned as an academician and restored to his former office.

sentences.zh: 偓不敢入朝，挈其族南依王審知而卒。

translations.literal: Wo dared not enter court, took his clan south to rely on Wang Shenzhi, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Wo dared not enter court. He took his clan south to place themselves under Wang Shenzhi and died there.

sentences.zh: 兄儀，字羽光，亦以翰林學士為御史中丞。

translations.literal: His elder brother Yi, style name Yuguang, also from Hanlin academician became Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Han Yi, whose courtesy name was Yuguang, likewise rose from Hanlin academician to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 偓貶之明年，帝宴文思球場，全忠入，百官坐廡下，全忠怒，貶儀棣州司馬，侍御史歸藹登州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: The year after Wo's demotion the emperor feasted at the Wensi ball ground; Quanzhong entered; the hundred officials sat beneath the corridor; Quanzhong was angry and demoted Yi to Militia Vice-Prefect of Di and Remonstrating Attendant Gui Ai to Registrar of Deng.
translations.idiomatic: In the year after Wo's demotion the emperor gave a feast at the Wensi ball ground. When Quanzhong entered, the officials were all seated beneath the corridor, and Quanzhong grew angry. He demoted Yi to militia vice-prefect of Di Prefecture and the remonstrating attendant Gui Ai to registrar of Deng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：懿、僖以來，王道日失厥序，腐尹塞朝，賢人遁逃，四方豪英，各附所合而奮。

translations.literal: The commentator says: From Yizong and Xizong onward the kingly way daily lost its order; corrupt functionaries filled the court; worthy men fled; heroes of the four quarters each attached to what suited them and rose up.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: From the reigns of Yizong and Xizong onward, the kingly way daily lost its proper order. Corrupt officials filled the court, worthy men fled into hiding, and heroes throughout the realm each attached themselves to whatever cause suited them and rose up in struggle.

sentences.zh: 天子塊然，所與者，惟佞愎庸奴，乃欲鄣橫流、支已顛，寧不殆哉！

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven stood alone; those he had were only flatterers, obstinate fools and slaves—yet he wished to block the rushing torrent and prop up his own collapse—would he not be imperiled!
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven stood isolated. Those around him were only flatterers, obstinate fools, and servile men. Yet he wished to block the rushing torrent and prop up a throne already toppling—how could he not be brought to ruin!

sentences.zh: 觀綮、朴輩不次而用，捭豚臑，拒貙牙，趣亡而已。

translations.literal: Observing Qi, Pu and their sort used out of order—flinging pig shanks, repelling leopard fangs—they merely hastened ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Consider how men like Qi and Pu were promoted out of turn: it was like flinging a pig shank at a leopard's fangs—nothing but a rush toward destruction.

sentences.zh: 一韓偓不能容，況賢者乎？

translations.literal: A single Han Wo could not be tolerated—how much less the worthy!
translations.idiomatic: If even a single Han Wo could not be tolerated, how much less could true men of worth!
